sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》旗下的每日新闻简报《Dealbook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的Dealbook峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、扎伊兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多嘉宾。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 你可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经剪辑的对话实况。

sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在nytimes.com上直播部分精选采访，供所有人免费观看。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望你能收看。

sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》节目。

sentences.en: Today,
sentences.zh: 今天，

sentences.en: Russian President Vladimir Putin has been elected to a fourth term with no real challenger and with support from more than three quarters of Russian voters.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京在没有真正竞争对手且获得超过四分之三俄罗斯选民支持的情况下，成功连任第四个任期。

sentences.en: How the most powerful man in Russia holds on to power.
sentences.zh: 这位俄罗斯最有权势的人是如何稳固权力的。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, March 20th.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月20日，星期二。

sentences.en: From ABC, this is World News Tonight with
sentences.zh: 这里是美国广播公司（ABC）的《世界新闻今夜》，我是

sentences.en: Peter Jennings, reporting tonight from Berlin.
sentences.zh: 彼得·詹宁斯，今晚从柏林为您报道。

sentences.en: From the Berlin Wall specifically, take a look at them.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，是在柏林墙边，看看他们。

sentences.en: They've been there since last night.
sentences.zh: 他们从昨晚就一直待在那里。

sentences.en: So it's the fall of 1989 and Europe is still divided in the Cold War, East and WeSt. Occasionally they shout, de mal muss veck, the wall must go.
sentences.zh: 那是1989年的秋天，欧洲仍处于冷战的对峙中，分为东西两部分。人们偶尔会高喊：“墙必须倒下”。

sentences.en: But that's about to end.
sentences.zh: 但这一切即将结束。

sentences.en: Mr. Gorbachev, tear down this wall.
sentences.zh: 戈尔巴乔夫先生，推倒这堵墙。

sentences.en: They're bringing down the wall piece by piece, officials and ordinary citizens.
sentences.zh: 他们正在一块一块地拆除这堵墙，有官员，也有普通市民。

sentences.en: And in November, the Berlin Wall comes down.
sentences.zh: 到了11月，柏林墙倒塌了。

sentences.en: Tonight, citizens from both Germanies are singing and dancing on the wall itself.
sentences.zh: 今晚，来自东西德的市民在墙上载歌载舞。

sentences.en: But some of the celebrants appear to have gone too far.
sentences.zh: 但一些庆祝者似乎做得太过火了。

sentences.en: That's the euphoria spread, the protest spread with it.
sentences.zh: 那是狂喜的蔓延，抗议也随之蔓延。

sentences.en: Tonight, the people had their revenge.
sentences.zh: 今晚，人民复仇了。

sentences.en: The people in East Germany were protesting the lack of freedom they wanted to have with the West had.
sentences.zh: 东德人民抗议他们缺乏自由，而他们渴望拥有西方那样的自由。

sentences.en: Personal freedom, it was economic freedom.
sentences.zh: 那是个人自由，也是经济自由。

sentences.en: East Germany was such a stifling place.
sentences.zh: 东德曾是一个令人窒息的地方。

sentences.en: As they gained momentum, they sort of gained confidence.
sentences.zh: 随着势头的增强，他们似乎也获得了信心。

sentences.en: And on the night of December 5th, almost a month after the wall comes down, a group of people decided that they would turn their attention to the KGB.
sentences.zh: 12月5日晚，即柏林墙倒塌近一个月后，一群人决定将矛头指向克格勃（KGB）。

sentences.en: You know, they were throwing off the Soviet-imposed system and saw the KGB as part of the enforcement.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们当时正在摆脱苏联强加的体制，并将克格勃视为该体制的执法工具。

sentences.en: Stephen Lee Myers covered Putin's rise as Moscow bureau chief for the Times.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬·李·迈尔斯曾作为《纽约时报》莫斯科分社社长报道过普京的崛起。

sentences.en: And it was at this moment that Vladimir Putin was serving as an officer in KGB, East Germany, for five years.
sentences.zh: 当时，弗拉基米尔·普京已经在东德担任了五年的克格勃军官。

sentences.en: And he watched all of this unfold.
sentences.zh: 他目睹了这一切的发生。

sentences.en: Tens of thousands of people gathered outside of this villa where Putin had worked.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的人聚集在普京工作的别墅外。

sentences.en: And Putin was there.
sentences.zh: 普京当时就在那里。

sentences.en: He was the deputy at the time.
sentences.zh: 他当时是副手。

sentences.en: And he didn't know what to do.
sentences.zh: 他不知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: At that point, I think there were four officers there with him.
sentences.zh: 当时我想他身边只有四名军官。

sentences.en: They probably would have been easily overwhelmed.
sentences.zh: 他们很可能会轻易地被人群淹没。

sentences.en: And he couldn't find his boss.
sentences.zh: 而且他找不到他的上司。

sentences.en: He didn't have orders.
sentences.zh: 他没有接到任何命令。

sentences.en: He kept calling for reinforcements to ask for direction, what to do, how to stop these protests, whether to stop these protests.
sentences.zh: 他不断请求增援，询问指示，该怎么做，如何阻止这些抗议，或者是否应该阻止这些抗议。

sentences.en: And the officer on the phone told Putin that Moscow was silent.
sentences.zh: 电话那头的军官告诉普京，莫斯科保持沉默。

sentences.en: And it was a devastating moment for Putin because he felt like the country that he served had no answer.
sentences.zh: 这对普京来说是一个毁灭性的时刻，因为他觉得他所效忠的国家对此毫无对策。

sentences.en: It was a sign of weakness for him that they were unable to act at this moment of great danger.
sentences.zh: 对他而言，这是一种软弱的信号，因为他们在如此危险的时刻竟然无法采取行动。

sentences.en: And the protesters were outside his building at this point.
sentences.zh: 此时抗议者就在他的大楼外。

sentences.en: And he had to decide what to do.
sentences.zh: 他必须决定怎么做。

sentences.en: And without orders, he went out and he bluffed.
sentences.zh: 在没有命令的情况下，他走了出去，虚张声势。

sentences.en: He said that he was an officer of the
sentences.zh: 他声称自己是

sentences.en: Soviet Union and that this was a diplomatic compound.
sentences.zh: 苏联的军官，这里是外交机构。

sentences.en: And that if they tried to enter, the guards would open fire.
sentences.zh: 如果他们试图闯入，守卫将会开火。

sentences.en: And that that was persuasive to the crowd.
sentences.zh: 这番话成功说服了人群。

sentences.en: So the the bluff worked?
sentences.zh: 所以，虚张声势奏效了？

sentences.en: It did.
sentences.zh: 确实奏效了。

sentences.en: And for Putin, it was a really important moment in life.
sentences.zh: 对普京来说，这是他人生中非常重要的时刻。

sentences.en: The takeaway for Putin, I think, has been that you have to show strength and you have to show resolve, even if there's not necessarily something to back that up.
sentences.zh: 我认为普京从中得到的教训是：你必须表现出力量和决心，即使你并没有真正的实力作为后盾。

sentences.en: The perception of strength is as important as the strength itself.
sentences.zh: 对力量的感知与力量本身同样重要。

sentences.en: How do you think the young Vladimir Putin got this idea?
sentences.zh: 你认为年轻的弗拉基米尔·普京是如何产生这种想法的？

sentences.en: Where does his story start?
sentences.zh: 他的故事是从哪里开始的？

sentences.en: He was born in 1952 in Leningrad, now St. Petersburg.
sentences.zh: 他1952年出生于列宁格勒，即现在的圣彼得堡。

sentences.en: He lived in a communal apartment with a bathroom down the hall.
sentences.zh: 他住在一间公共公寓里，走廊尽头才有洗手间。

sentences.en: It was infested with rats.
sentences.zh: 那里鼠患成灾。

sentences.en: But nonetheless, he grew up with a very romantic notion of the Soviet Union as a great power.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，他在成长过程中对苏联作为大国怀有一种非常浪漫的憧憬。

sentences.en: The Second World War broke out in 1939.
sentences.zh: 第二次世界大战于1939年爆发。

sentences.en: And in 1941, Germany attacked the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 1941年，德国进攻苏联。

sentences.en: At that point, the city was still very much like the country, rebuilding from the devastation of the war.
sentences.zh: 当时，这座城市和整个国家一样，仍在从战争的蹂躏中重建。

sentences.en: The destruction was enormous.
sentences.zh: 破坏是巨大的。

sentences.en: But the war gave people a renewed spirit of patriotism and unity.
sentences.zh: 但战争赋予了人们一种重燃的爱国主义和团结精神。

sentences.en: They had defeated Nazi Germany.
sentences.zh: 他们击败了纳粹德国。

sentences.en: So for many people in the Soviet Union, it became a great source of pride.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于苏联的许多人来说，这成为了巨大的自豪感来源。

sentences.en: When peace came, the Soviet Union emerged as the strongest nation in Europe.
sentences.zh: 和平到来时，苏联成为了欧洲最强大的国家。

sentences.en: And then there was a sense of rejuvenation, I think, that the Soviet Union was beginning to achieve its promises.
sentences.zh: 我认为当时有一种重获新生的感觉，觉得苏联开始实现它的承诺了。

sentences.en: We in the West had expected that the United States would be the first to launch a satellite.
sentences.zh: 我们西方人曾预计美国会率先发射卫星。

sentences.en: Well, now the Russians have done it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，现在俄罗斯人做到了。

sentences.en: They've done it first and they've done it with complete success.
sentences.zh: 他们率先做到了，而且取得了圆满成功。

sentences.en: It put a satellite in space and then a man in space.
sentences.zh: 它将卫星送入了太空，随后又将人类送入了太空。

sentences.en: As a teenager, there was a movie that came out called
sentences.zh: 青少年时期，有一部电影上映了，叫作

sentences.en: The Sword and the Shield.
sentences.zh: 《盾与剑》。

sentences.en: And he was absolutely enchanted by this movie.
sentences.zh: 他被这部电影深深迷住了。

sentences.en: It was a story of an agent from the
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于一名来自

sentences.en: Soviet Union who spoke German and who managed to infiltrate the Nazi army.
sentences.zh: 苏联的特工的故事，他会说德语，并成功打入了纳粹军队内部。

sentences.en: And Putin was so enchanted with this as he tells the story that he went immediately the next day to try to volunteer for the KGB.
sentences.zh: 据普京自己讲述，他当时被深深吸引，第二天就立刻去申请加入克格勃。

sentences.en: That was the kind of romantic young man he was.
sentences.zh: 他就是那样一个浪漫的年轻人。

sentences.en: And they, of course, didn't take him.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们没有录取他。

sentences.en: They don't accept walk-ons in the KGB.
sentences.zh: 克格勃是不接受主动上门的申请的。

sentences.en: But nonetheless, I think the seed was planted and he went off to university.
sentences.zh: 但尽管如此，我认为种子已经种下，他后来去上了大学。

sentences.en: And while he was in university, he was then approached by the KGB, which is how it works.
sentences.zh: 在大学期间，他被克格勃招募了，这就是他们的运作方式。

sentences.en: And he signed up.
sentences.zh: 于是他加入了。

sentences.en: In 1983, he's given a chance to go to the KGB finishing school that prepared agents to go abroad.
sentences.zh: 1983年，他获得了进入克格勃进修学校的机会，该校专门培养派往国外的特工。

sentences.en: And instead of getting a dream assignment to West Germany or Austria or Switzerland, he ends up in East Germany, in Dresden, a kind of outpoSt.
sentences.zh: 但他没有得到梦寐以求的西德、奥地利或瑞士的职位，而是被派往了东德的德累斯顿，一个偏远的前哨站。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So not a glamorous position.
sentences.zh: 所以那不是什么光鲜的职位。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's official.
sentences.zh: 官方消息确认了。

sentences.en: Germany is now one country of 80 million people.
sentences.zh: 德国现在是一个拥有8000万人口的国家。

sentences.en: You know, when the East Germany fell and the Soviet Union began to pull out its agents like him.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当东德倒台，苏联开始撤回像他这样的特工时。

sentences.en: Unlike the Western allies who leave to a fanfare next week, the departure of the Russian troops will be low key.
sentences.zh: 与下周将伴随欢呼声离开的西方盟军不同，俄罗斯军队的撤离将非常低调。

sentences.en: They may have liberated Berlin from the Nazis, but for 50 years, they also surrounded the city with communism.
sentences.zh: 他们或许曾将柏林从纳粹手中解放出来，但50年来，他们也用共产主义包围了这座城市。

sentences.en: When Putin comes home, there's a sense of embarrassment.
sentences.zh: 当普京回国时，有一种尴尬的感觉。

sentences.en: The country is in chaos.
sentences.zh: 国家陷入了混乱。

sentences.en: Putin can't really find much of a job because lots of KGB officers who are coming home all of a sudden from all over the world.
sentences.zh: 普京很难找到一份像样的工作，因为大量克格勃军官突然从世界各地回国。

sentences.en: And he has to move back with his wife and now two daughters into the apartment of his parents.
sentences.zh: 他不得不带着妻子和两个女儿搬回父母的公寓居住。

sentences.en: He's 37 years old.
sentences.zh: 他当时37岁。

sentences.en: And this country that he believes in, that he served as an officer of, is in complete chaos.
sentences.zh: 而这个他所信仰、曾作为军官效忠的国家，正处于彻底的混乱之中。

sentences.en: So the image Putin had of his country is gone.
sentences.zh: 所以普京心中对国家的形象破灭了。

sentences.en: The country now kind of has its tail between its legs.
sentences.zh: 这个国家现在有点垂头丧气。

sentences.en: The Soviet ideology that he had so bought into seems dead at this point.
sentences.zh: 他曾经深信不疑的苏联意识形态，此时似乎已经死亡。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: St. Petersburg, a city once famous for its 18th century elegance and culture, is now a victim of its recent past and the transition to a new order.
sentences.zh: 圣彼得堡，这座曾经以18世纪的优雅和文化而闻名的城市，现在成了其近期历史和向新秩序转型过程中的受害者。

sentences.en: The Soviet communist experiment is failing at this point.
sentences.zh: 苏联的共产主义实验此时正在失败。

sentences.en: Today, it's the scene for some of the most disturbing social problems to be found in Russia.
sentences.zh: 今天，这里成了俄罗斯最令人不安的社会问题的缩影。

sentences.en: And what happens is Boris Yeltsin emerges as the first president of a new Russia.
sentences.zh: 随后发生的事情是，鲍里斯·叶利钦成为了新俄罗斯的第一任总统。

sentences.en: It's a sight that both excites and frightens those in the Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 这一景象让苏联国内的人们既兴奋又恐惧。

sentences.en: For the first time in 70 years, the Soviet leadership was allowing multi-candidate elections for a powerful body.
sentences.zh: 70年来，苏联领导层首次允许为一个强力机构进行多候选人选举。

sentences.en: And sets about transforming it into a democratic and capitalist country.
sentences.zh: 并着手将其转型为一个民主和资本主义国家。

sentences.en: And he did so in a sometimes referred to as shock therapy.
sentences.zh: 他采取了一种有时被称为“休克疗法”的手段。

sentences.en: We need millions of property owners and not just a few millionaires.
sentences.zh: 我们需要数百万的财产所有者，而不仅仅是几个百万富翁。

sentences.en: All Russian citizens, workers, pensioners and small children will be given privatization vouchers worth 10,000 rubles.
sentences.zh: 所有俄罗斯公民，包括工人、养老金领取者和小孩子，都将获得价值1万卢布的私有化凭证。

sentences.en: What you had is this very abrupt transition from an economy where everything was planned for you, even where you worked, to one where you were on your own.
sentences.zh: 你所经历的是从一种一切都为你规划好（甚至包括你在哪里工作）的经济，向一种必须自谋生路的经济的剧烈转型。

sentences.en: And you had to find your own job and you had to find your own ways to get money.
sentences.zh: 你必须自己找工作，自己想办法赚钱。

sentences.en: And for a lot of people, it was a tremendously difficult transition.
sentences.zh: 对很多人来说，这是一个极其艰难的转型。

sentences.en: As the economic crisis deepens, so the number of the destitute and desperate pouring into the capital has steadily increased.
sentences.zh: 随着经济危机的加深，涌入首都的赤贫和绝望的人数稳步增加。

sentences.en: A lot of people, frankly, starved.
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，很多人挨饿了。

sentences.en: Hundreds of thousands more are fleeing from the ethnic unrest in various former Soviet republics.
sentences.zh: 还有成千上万的人从前苏联各加盟共和国的民族动乱中逃离出来。

sentences.en: Many arrive at the train stations and never leave.
sentences.zh: 许多人抵达火车站后就再也没有离开。

sentences.en: People who had connections, you know, they were able to thrive in this system.
sentences.zh: 那些有关系的人，你知道，他们能够在这种体制下如鱼得水。

sentences.en: And so from this, you had the so-called oligarchs who amassed these tremendous fortunes by taking over state enterprises, especially oil and minerals and things like that.
sentences.zh: 因此，由此产生了所谓的“寡头”，他们通过接管国有企业（尤其是石油、矿产等）积累了巨额财富。

sentences.en: But many others suffered through this transition.
sentences.zh: 但许多其他人却在这次转型中饱受煎熬。

sentences.en: It was a very difficult time in the 90s.
sentences.zh: 90年代是一个非常艰难的时期。

sentences.en: It was a very violent time.
sentences.zh: 那是一个非常暴力的时期。

sentences.en: And, you know, Boris Yeltsin, who was in his heart a Democrat and wanted to make this transition, was also a weak leader in many ways.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，鲍里斯·叶利钦，他内心是一位民主主义者，想要推动这种转型，但在许多方面也是一位软弱的领导人。

sentences.en: And he was overwhelmed by the influence of these oligarchs.
sentences.zh: 他被这些寡头的影响力所压倒。

sentences.en: And himself was known for heavy drinking and was ill as well.
sentences.zh: 他本人也以酗酒闻名，而且身体状况不佳。

sentences.en: And, you know, it made him a very ineffectual leader, especially towards the end of the 90s.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这使他成为了一位非常无能的领导人，尤其是在90年代末期。

sentences.en: So where is Putin in all of this?
sentences.zh: 那么普京在这一切中处于什么位置？

sentences.en: So when Putin comes back from East Germany, he eventually leaves the KGB.
sentences.zh: 当普京从东德回来后，他最终离开了克格勃。

sentences.en: He joins the democratic government and rises through the ranks there.
sentences.zh: 他加入了民主政府，并在那里步步高升。

sentences.en: And in 96, he moves to Moscow and begins to make his way into and up the Yeltsin presidential administration.
sentences.zh: 1996年，他搬到莫斯科，开始进入并跻身叶利钦的总统行政团队。

sentences.en: Eventually, he gets a job because of his background in the KGB, leading the new successor agency of the KGB, which is called the Federal Security Service, the FSB.
sentences.zh: 最终，凭借在克格勃的背景，他获得了一份工作，领导克格勃的继任机构，即联邦安全局（FSB）。

sentences.en: And Putin takes over this job at a time when Yeltsin's facing great political peril.
sentences.zh: 普京接手这份工作时，叶利钦正面临巨大的政治危机。

sentences.en: There's an investigation into corruption that's inching closer and closer to him and his family.
sentences.zh: 一项腐败调查正一步步逼近他和他的家人。

sentences.en: And then one night, late at night on TV, a video appears.
sentences.zh: 然后有一天深夜，电视上出现了一段视频。

sentences.en: And it shows the investigator who is leading the charge against Yeltsin having sex with a woman who's not his wife.
sentences.zh: 视频显示，那位领导针对叶利钦调查的调查员，正与一名非其妻子的女性发生性关系。

sentences.en: By all accounts, the source of the tape was Vladimir Putin.
sentences.zh: 据各方说法，这段录像的来源是弗拉基米尔·普京。

sentences.en: And it helps bring down the chief investigator.
sentences.zh: 这有助于扳倒那位首席调查员。

sentences.en: And it was seen by Yeltsin as a tremendous act of loyalty.
sentences.zh: 叶利钦将其视为一种极大的忠诚表现。

sentences.en: So, what happens to Putin after that?
sentences.zh: 那么，在那之后普京发生了什么？

sentences.en: It's not long after this that Yeltsin reshuffles his government again.
sentences.zh: 没过多久，叶利钦再次改组了政府。

sentences.en: And this time he turns to Putin to be his new prime minister.
sentences.zh: 这一次，他选择了普京作为他的新任总理。

sentences.en: Boris Yeltsin, overnight, told the Russian people he's resigning and that Mr. Putin, the prime minister, has all the powers.
sentences.zh: 鲍里斯·叶利钦一夜之间告诉俄罗斯人民他要辞职，而总理普京拥有所有权力。

sentences.en: And what happens when Putin gets into office as president?
sentences.zh: 那么，当普京就任总统后发生了什么？

sentences.en: I think Putin understood early on that the most important thing he could do was create a new narrative for people to feel pride again in the country.
sentences.zh: 我认为普京很早就明白，他能做的最重要的事情就是创造一种新的叙事，让人们重新为这个国家感到自豪。

sentences.en: The first order of business is to reassert the control of the state, the power and authority of the government.
sentences.zh: 首要任务是重申国家控制权，以及政府的权力和权威。

sentences.en: And then he also imposed control over the media.
sentences.zh: 然后，他还加强了对媒体的控制。

sentences.en: He saw from the very beginning that especially television was important to not only his own power.
sentences.zh: 他从一开始就看出，电视尤其重要，不仅是为了他自己的权力。

sentences.en: Projecting this image of himself as a strong leader, but also of the country.
sentences.zh: 不仅要投射出他作为强力领导人的形象，也要投射出国家的形象。

sentences.en: And it was very powerful.
sentences.zh: 这非常有影响力。

sentences.en: And from this, you saw the creation of this image of Putin as the young, fit president doing judo, riding horseback, diving and flying, in some ways, crude propaganda.
sentences.zh: 由此，你看到了普京形象的塑造：年轻、健壮的总统，会柔道、骑马、潜水、开飞机，在某种程度上，这是一种粗糙的宣传。

sentences.en: But it was very powerful.
sentences.zh: 但它非常有效。

sentences.en: So, that image we all have of Putin shirtless, barrel-chested on a horse, that was very much by design, a projection of strength and pride.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们所有人脑海中普京赤裸上身、胸肌发达骑马的形象，很大程度上是刻意设计的，是对力量和自豪感的投射。

sentences.en: People wanted a savior who could let them feel good again about their country and what they stood for and what they believed in.
sentences.zh: 人们想要一位救世主，能让他们重新为自己的国家、所代表的立场和信仰感到自豪。

sentences.en: The amazing thing is that this worked.
sentences.zh: 令人惊奇的是，这奏效了。

sentences.en: After years of the embarrassments of Yeltsin and the chaos of the 90s, people were really attracted to this new leader.
sentences.zh: 在经历了叶利钦时代的尴尬和90年代的混乱之后，人们真的被这位新领导人吸引了。

sentences.en: Wrote songs about him.
sentences.zh: 还为他写了歌。

sentences.en: And there was one pop hit called Takovokok Putin, a man like Putin, who would be a good boyfriend, a good husband, you know, somebody who didn't beat her,
sentences.zh: 有一首流行金曲叫《像普京那样的人》，歌词说他会是个好男友、好丈夫，你知道的，一个不会打她的人，

sentences.en: somebody who didn't drink.
sentences.zh: 一个不酗酒的人。

sentences.en: And it was genuine, I think.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是真诚的。

sentences.en: Some of this, of course, is generated by loyalists and the media.
sentences.zh: 当然，其中一些是由忠诚者和媒体制造出来的。

sentences.en: But I think people really responded positively to this new image of Russia embodied by Putin himself.
sentences.zh: 但我认为人们确实对普京本人所体现的这种俄罗斯新形象做出了积极回应。

sentences.en: So, he succeeded in reshaping the narrative inside of Russia by projecting this image of a strongman leader.
sentences.zh: 所以，他通过投射这种强人领导者的形象，成功地重塑了俄罗斯内部的叙事。

sentences.en: And he begins to do the same thing on the international stage.
sentences.zh: 然后他开始在国际舞台上做同样的事情。

sentences.en: Putin has increasingly put himself at odds with the international community, particularly the United States, by pushing the limits of what he can get away with.
sentences.zh: 普京通过不断挑战他所能容忍的底线，日益将自己置于与国际社会，特别是美国对立的境地。

sentences.en: You saw that when he annexed Crimea from Ukraine in 2014.
sentences.zh: 你在2014年他吞并克里米亚时就看到了这一点。

sentences.en: Violence in eastern Ukraine today as pro-Russia demonstrators stormed the Ukrainian security building.
sentences.zh: 今天乌克兰东部发生暴力事件，亲俄示威者冲击了乌克兰安全局大楼。

sentences.en: Fears are now growing from a large-scale Russian invasion.
sentences.zh: 人们现在越来越担心发生大规模的俄罗斯入侵。

sentences.en: When he intervened in Syria a year later.
sentences.zh: 当他一年后干预叙利亚时。

sentences.en: Russia's deployment of troops and equipment outside its own borders now in Syria is the largest since the end of the Cold War.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯在境外部署军队和装备，这是自冷战结束以来规模最大的一次。

sentences.en: The United States and Russia are on opposite sides of Syria's war, make no mistake.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，美国和俄罗斯站在了叙利亚战争的对立面。

sentences.en: And then the biggest example came with the American election in 2016.
sentences.zh: 然后，最大的例子出现在2016年的美国大选中。

sentences.en: Did Russia meddle in the 2016 elections?
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯干预了2016年大选吗？

sentences.en: Russia did meddle in the election.
sentences.zh: 俄罗斯确实干预了选举。

sentences.en: That's according to top officials in the CIA, FBI, and NSA.
sentences.zh: 这是中央情报局、联邦调查局和国家安全局的高级官员所说的。

sentences.en: It is an unprecedented response to Russia's suspected cyber attack on our country.
sentences.zh: 这是对俄罗斯涉嫌对我国进行网络攻击的前所未有的回应。

sentences.en: Today, President Obama made good on that promise to retaliate, targeting Russia's top intelligence agencies with sanctions.
sentences.zh: 今天，奥巴马总统兑现了报复的承诺，对俄罗斯顶级情报机构实施了制裁。

sentences.en: Sanctions on Russia would come in response to Russian meddling in the election.
sentences.zh: 对俄罗斯的制裁是对俄罗斯干预选举的回应。

sentences.en: And what is he signaling, Putin, in this latest and arguably biggest provocation by meddling in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 那么，普京在这次最新且可以说是最大的挑衅中，通过干预美国

sentences.en: elections?
sentences.zh: 选举，是在释放什么信号？

sentences.en: I think he's signaling that he can act wherever he wants, including in the United States, with impunity.
sentences.zh: 我认为他是在释放信号，表明他可以在任何他想行动的地方，包括在美国，肆无忌惮地行事。

sentences.en: Is this also about portraying the West as an adversary to Russians?
sentences.zh: 这也是为了将西方描绘成俄罗斯人的对手吗？

sentences.en: I think it's all about portraying the West as an adversary.
sentences.zh: 我认为这完全是为了将西方描绘成对手。

sentences.en: The extent that Putin can create the image for Russian people of an enemy at the gates, a sense of being under siege, it emboldens him, it builds his support.
sentences.zh: 普京越能为俄罗斯人民营造出一种大敌当前的形象，一种被围困的感觉，就越能壮大他的胆量，巩固他的支持率。

sentences.en: And even when the United States reacts with more sanctions or more criticism, it just reinforces the idea.
sentences.zh: 即使美国以更多的制裁或更多的批评作为回应，也只会强化这一观念。

sentences.en: So he's created a cycle where the provocation makes him popular, and then the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以他创造了一个循环，挑衅让他变得受欢迎，然后美国的

sentences.en: counter-response makes him even more popular.
sentences.zh: 反制措施让他变得更受欢迎。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's like it proves his point to the Russian people.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就像是向俄罗斯人民证明了他的观点。

sentences.en: Of course, they hammer that idea home.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们会反复强调这个观点。

sentences.en: They're hearing that Vladimir Putin is protecting them from enemies abroad.
sentences.zh: 他们听到的是弗拉基米尔·普京正在保护他们免受外部敌人的侵害。

sentences.en: And the main enemy, of course, being the United States, that the West generally are trying to keep Russia weak.
sentences.zh: 而主要的敌人当然是美国，即西方国家总体上试图让俄罗斯保持虚弱。

sentences.en: It seems like what you're saying is that a central component of Putin's strategy is that the West is Russia's enemy, and that that's the reason why Russia needs a strong leader,
sentences.zh: 你似乎是在说，普京战略的核心组成部分是西方是俄罗斯的敌人，而这就是俄罗斯需要一位强力领导人的原因，

sentences.en: that that's why they need Putin.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们需要普京的原因。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: It's almost as if without Putin, the country would be overrun by the forces of the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 就好像如果没有普京，这个国家就会被西方的势力所蹂躏。

sentences.en: So I'm wondering then, could Putin have accumulated as much power as he has without having cast the West as the enemy?
sentences.zh: 那么我很好奇，如果普京没有把西方塑造成敌人，他还能积累到今天这么大的权力吗？

sentences.en: That's a great question, and it's hard to answer.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的问题，很难回答。

sentences.en: I think in the end, if it hadn't been the U.S., he would have found another enemy.
sentences.zh: 我认为最终，如果不是美国，他也会找到另一个敌人。

sentences.en: Because I think it's become essential to the image, to the political model that he's created, that only a strong leader can govern Russia at this point.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为这对他所创造的形象和政治模式来说已经变得至关重要，即在目前的情况下，只有强力领导人才能治理俄罗斯。

sentences.en: That only a strong leader stands between the country and chaos.
sentences.zh: 只有强力领导人才能在国家和混乱之间筑起防线。

sentences.en: Do you think that Russia meddling in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 你认为俄罗斯干预美国

sentences.en: election and the success of that is the ultimate realization of the story from East Germany that you told us at the beginning of our conversation?
sentences.zh: 选举及其成功，是你谈话开始时讲的那个东德故事的最终实现吗？

sentences.en: Is this another example of Putin showing that if you're bold enough and if you display enough resolve, it's possible to have an outsized impact with arguably minimal effort?
sentences.zh: 这是普京展示的另一个例子吗：如果你足够大胆，表现出足够的决心，就有可能以极小的代价产生巨大的影响？

sentences.en: I think Putin is saying very clearly that he will do whatever it takes to protect Russian interests, even if that means standing up to the United States directly.
sentences.zh: 我认为普京非常明确地表示，他会不惜一切代价保护俄罗斯的利益，即使这意味着直接对抗美国。

sentences.en: You know, Russia remains a superpower, a nuclear power, and they even talk now about new weapons that they're developing.
sentences.zh: 你知道，俄罗斯仍然是一个超级大国，一个核大国，他们现在甚至在谈论正在开发的新型武器。

sentences.en: The question we have to answer is, is he prepared to use them?
sentences.zh: 我们需要回答的问题是，他准备好使用它们了吗？

sentences.en: And we just don't know that.
sentences.zh: 我们只是不知道。

sentences.en: Stephen, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: On Sunday, in Russia's presidential election, Vladimir Putin won 76% of the vote, despite barely bothering to campaign,
sentences.zh: 周日，在俄罗斯总统大选中，弗拉基米尔·普京赢得了76%的选票，尽管他几乎没怎么费心竞选，

sentences.en: except to stress that Russia is under siege and he is the man to keep it safe by projecting power beyond its borders.
sentences.zh: 除了强调俄罗斯正处于被围困状态，而他是通过向境外投射力量来保障国家安全的人。

sentences.en: To emphasize that point, Election Day was moved to March 18th, the fourth anniversary of Russia's seizure of Crimea.
sentences.zh: 为了强调这一点，选举日被改到了3月18日，即俄罗斯夺取克里米亚四周年纪念日。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Marc Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·朗森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个关于热爱设计及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在黑胶唱片时代在夜店当DJ的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 每天晚上你都要带着300件你最珍贵的财产去上班，把DJ台变成一个充满50年历史精美文物的活生生的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，而且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你第一次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间越过付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能得到什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，免费获取30天的访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: Joe DiGenova is a former U.S.
sentences.zh: 乔·迪杰诺瓦是前美国

sentences.en: attorney in D.C.
sentences.zh: 哥伦比亚特区联邦检察官，

sentences.en: and he joins us tonight.
sentences.zh: 他今晚加入我们的节目。

sentences.en: Joe, thanks a lot for coming on.
sentences.zh: 乔，非常感谢你能来。

sentences.en: My pleasure.
sentences.zh: 我的荣幸。

sentences.en: The Times reports that President Trump has decided to hire a longtime Washington lawyer, Joseph DiGenova,
sentences.zh: 《时报》报道称，特朗普总统已决定聘请资深华盛顿律师约瑟夫·迪杰诺瓦，

sentences.en: who has pushed the theory in interviews that the Russia investigation was concocted by FBI agents who wanted to prevent Trump from becoming president.
sentences.zh: 他在采访中提出了一种理论，即俄罗斯调查是由那些想要阻止特朗普成为总统的联邦调查局特工捏造的。

sentences.en: Make no mistake about it.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: A group of FBI and DOJ people were trying to frame Donald Trump of a falsely created crime.
sentences.zh: 一群联邦调查局和司法部的人试图给唐纳德·特朗普安上一个虚构的罪名。

sentences.en: DiGenova is not expected to take a lead role on the president's legal team,
sentences.zh: 预计迪杰诺瓦不会在总统的法律团队中担任领导角色，

sentences.en: but will serve as a more aggressive and outspoken figure at a time when Trump is openly attacking special counsel Robert Mueller's investigation.
sentences.zh: 但在特朗普公开攻击特别检察官罗伯特·穆勒的调查之际，他将作为一个更具攻击性和直言不讳的人物出现。

sentences.en: What would be the motive for that?
sentences.zh: 这样做的动机是什么？

sentences.en: The motive would be that they didn't like Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 动机是他们不喜欢唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: They didn't think he was fit to be president.
sentences.zh: 他们认为他不适合担任总统。

sentences.en: And they were going to do everything within their power to exonerate Hillary Clinton.
sentences.zh: 他们会尽其所能为希拉里·克林顿开脱。

sentences.en: And if she lost, to frame Donald Trump with a false crime because they didn't think he should be president.
sentences.zh: 如果她输了，就给唐纳德·特朗普安上一个虚假的罪名，因为他们认为他不应该当总统。

sentences.en: And.
sentences.zh: 而且。

sentences.en: Based on the preliminary review that we have done at this time, we have seen similarities in the device that exploded here last night
sentences.zh: 根据我们目前所做的初步审查，我们发现昨晚在这里爆炸的装置与

sentences.en: and the other three devices that have exploded in Austin starting on March 2nd.
sentences.zh: 自3月2日起在奥斯汀爆炸的其他三个装置有相似之处。

sentences.en: Police in Austin say that four explosions from packages left across the city over the past month appear to be the work of a serial bomber who is showing increasing sophistication.
sentences.zh: 奥斯汀警方表示，过去一个月在全市范围内留下的包裹引发的四起爆炸，似乎是一个连环炸弹客所为，且其手段日益复杂。

sentences.en: The latest attack was set off by a tripwire on a residential street.
sentences.zh: 最近的一次袭击是由一条住宅街道上的绊线触发的。

sentences.en: The previous three bombings all involved packages dropped at people's homes.
sentences.zh: 前三次爆炸都涉及投放在人们家门口的包裹。

sentences.en: So far, the bombings have killed two people and injured four more.
sentences.zh: 到目前为止，这些爆炸已造成两人死亡，四人受伤。

sentences.en: These events in Austin have garnered worldwide attention and we assure you that we are listening.
sentences.zh: 奥斯汀发生的这些事件引起了全世界的关注，我们向你们保证，我们正在倾听。

sentences.en: At a news conference before Sunday's explosion, Austin police made a rare public appeal for those responsible for the bombings to contact the police and explain their motives.
sentences.zh: 在周日爆炸发生前的新闻发布会上，奥斯汀警方罕见地公开呼吁爆炸案的责任人联系警方并解释他们的动机。

sentences.en: We want to understand what brought you to this point and we want to listen to you.
sentences.zh: 我们想了解是什么让你走到了这一步，我们想听听你的心声。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是今天的《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine until this summer
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个严密控制的机器运作，直到今年夏天

sentences.en: when elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一群自称改革者的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，该党就陷入了一场伤痕累累、混乱不堪，有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在我和莎拉·凯尼格主持的最新一期《地铁》节目中，讲述了人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
